text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Public servants in the capital Lusaka and in the northern mining towns of Kitwe and Ndola resolve to go on strike to push for better conditions of service.
- Scores of students at a secondary school in Lusaka riot in attempt to block police from arresting their headmaster for defying a local court order.
- The human rights commission says it has secured the release of 14 South Africans detained for straying into the international airport at an odd hour.
- A Burundese refugee is sentenced to five years imprisonment for rape.
- Deputy finance minister Godfrey Simasiku says government is unable to meet outstanding financial obligations because its coffers are dry.
- Donor representatives urge the government to adequately fund the newly-constituted human rights commission.
